pairs.question: Quid hoc est rei? cur non agnosco, Caecili, alacritatem tuam illam et illam oculorum etiam in seriis hilaritatem requiro?
pairs.answer: Iam dudum me Octavi nostri acriter angit et remordet oratio, qua in te invectus obiurgavit neglegentiae, ut me dissimulanter gravius argueret inscientiae.
pairs.derivation: Direct-speech exchange. Marcus (the narrator) asks why Caecilius has lost his cheerfulness; Caecilius answers that Octavius's speech has been gnawing at him. Dropped the narrative speech-tags 'Cui ego:' before the question and 'Tum ille:' before the answer. Answer-window: kept only Caecilius's operative first sentence, which directly states why he is downcast; cut at the first full stop, before 'Itaque progrediar ulterius...', where he stops answering and turns to proposing that he debate Octavius. Question is a real interrogative (Quid... cur...?). No words altered, added, or reordered.
